## The Three Layers

The GPS classification system asks three questions about every piece of evidence:

| Layer | Question | Options |
|---|---|---|
| **Source** | What kind of document is this? | Original / Derivative / Authored Work |
| **Information** | What did the informant know, and when? | Primary / Secondary / Indeterminate |
| **Evidence** | Does this fact directly answer the research question? | Direct / Indirect / Negative |

---

## Assertions by Source — Original vs. Derivative

### ✅ Original Sources (9 assertions)

These are documents created at the time the event occurred, or are images of the original record rather than re-keyed transcriptions.

### ⚠️ Derivative Sources (2 assertions)

These come from **src_002**, the **Ancestry.com index** of the 1850 census — a transcription derived from the original, not the original image itself. Transcription errors are possible, which is why this was used only as a cross-check.

| ID | Fact | Notes |

## Assertions by Information — Primary vs. Secondary vs. Indeterminate

### 🟢 Primary Information (2 assertions)

The informant had **firsthand knowledge** of the fact at the time it was recorded.

| ID | Fact | Informant | Why Primary |
|---|---|---|---|
